text:
sara.b: Quick heads-up — after the packing change landed, p50 on AWQ int8 (group_size=64) jumped ~18% on 2048-seqlen tests. Triage below.

miguel: ugh, saw that on canary too. Did you repro with/without KV cache warm?

sara.b: repro with cold and warm; warm shows less but still +10%. Traces attached (see perf-bot).

perf-bot: CPU profile snapshot: top 5 symbols: pack_unroll, kv_read, int8_matmul_kernel_v2, batch_router, kv_miss_handler
perf-bot: allocs: pack_buffer(45%), kv_cache(22%), matmul_workspace(18%)

dave_r: pack_unroll dominating. Maybe group-aware packing + smaller slab sizes will help. What's current slab_size? (asked)

sara.b: slab_size=256 by default, group_size=64. If we reduce slab to 128 overhead drops but more fragmentation.

jen-k: another angle: kernel selector picks int8_matmul_kernel_v2 for long seqs but it has worse prefetch pattern when pack buffers are large. Need perf guard: if pack_buffer > X bytes prefer kernel_v1.

miguel: Agree. Also batching heuristic: continuous batching increases effective seq length distribution -> triggers different code path in kernel chooser. We should add a lightweight heuristic to compute "effective_kv_density" and route.

sara.b: can we try kernel threshold change + slab reduction? I can run a 12-hour sweep on canary, would that be ok?

dave_r: yes, and add an ablation: AWQ calib mode on vs off — calibration influences scaling factors and that touches kernel paths.

miguel: I'll add a perf counter to measure pack_unroll calls per request and kv_cache_miss_ratio.

jen-k: Also consider packing lazy-emit: only pack when request likely to reuse prefix (use a short LRU window). That might reduce pack overhead for one-offs.

sara.b: test plan: 1) slab_size 128, 2) kernel threshold favor v1 when pack_buffer > 1MB, 3) lazy packing window=30s, 4) calib_on/off. Run 10k ops/day load generator.

perf-bot: started job: /jobs/1801234567/awq-packing-sweep
perf-bot: baseline metrics: p50=24ms p95=120ms cost=0.78 tokens/s  (timestamp 1801234567)

miguel: also log nvprof-ish counters: L2_miss, dram_read_bytes.

sara.b: quick log snippet from a regressed req:
```
[profile] req=abcd1234 seq=2048 group=64 slab=256 pack_buf=1.2MB kernel=v2 time=36ms
stack: pack_unroll -> int8_matmul_kernel_v2 -> kv_read -> batch_router
```

dave_r: can you also capture gdb sample to see prefetch distance? v2 uses prefetch stride=64 currently.

jen-k: If this is a cache-alignment problem, smaller group_size might help even if quant quality small hit. Any eval regressions expected?

sara.b: eval with 100 prompts shows negligible quality delta for group=32 vs 64 on AWQ, so tradeoff looks ok.

miguel: I'll PR kernel chooser: prefer v1 when pack_buf>1MB or group_size>128 or seq>1500. Add telemetry flag to flip.

sara.b: thanks. After we have sweep results I'll post summary. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: job finished: p50 change by config:
- slab128 + kernel_v1_if_pack>1MB => p50 -9%
- lazy_pack=30s => p50 -6%
- calib_off => p50 +2% (quality drop negligible)
final: best config slab=128, kernel heuristic, lazy_pack => p50 -14% p95 -10% cost -7%

miguel: nice. let's ship as canary config and monitor for regressions.

dave_r: add unit test for pack_unroll path and a perf regression alert.

jen-k: I'll update optimize recommendations and note calibration caveat.

sara.b: filed followups: #issues 8023 (kernel chooser), 8024 (packing config), 8025 (telemetry). Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
